params.message:
web-browse reads the longest-waiting page first, says why a fetch failed, and the scout proposes only addresses that answer

The page list began one place further every six hours while one round
reads many pages, so a page was read in a few rounds in a row and then
not until the start came round the whole list. On 25 November 2026 nine
sources on the failing list had been tried last on 9 November, with two
or three failures each: too few to be parked. Pages are now read
longest waiting first (last_collect_at), a page never read before all.

A failed fetch was stored as undici's bare "fetch failed"; it now names
the cause (no such host, no connection, a certificate for another
name), and a timeout says "no answer in 15 s". A host that is gone does
not park sooner: our own DNS can fail too.

The scout's model puts "www." in front of names that have none (Eye on
Design, Gorilla vs Bear) and the scout never looked at the page itself.
core/reachable.mjs asks the page first: any answer counts, a "www." is
dropped when only the bare name answers, and an address nothing answers
at is not proposed.

Portal: Webpagina's die de Observatory leest komen nu allemaal op hun beurt, een mislukte lezing zegt waarom, en de scout stelt geen bron meer voor op een adres dat niet bestaat.
